title: For a big tt-category whose compacts are local, reducedness of the fibre of the comparison map over zero is equivalent to a nilpotence alternative for two composable maps of compacts with vanishing tensor product
author: Paul Balmer
work: Homological support of big objects in tensor-triangulated categories
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 7 (2020), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.135
difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the theorem at source lines 881-893, label Thm:hom-local, printed as Theorem A.1: for a big tt-category whose compact-rigid subcategory is local, the assertion that the fibre of the comparison map from the homological to the triangular spectrum over zero is a single point is equivalent to a nilpotence alternative, namely that whenever two maps f and g of compacts satisfy f tensor g = 0, one of them is tensor-nilpotent on some non-zero compact. The proof at source lines 895-907 constructs the bridge between the two statements rather than observing it: in one direction it builds the Serre tensor-ideal B_0 of finitely presented modules admitting a non-zero compact that kills them, verifies closure under extensions from locality of the compacts, passes to the Gabriel quotient, and proves that a maximal tensor-ideal of the quotient has zero preimage in the compacts exactly when it contains B_0, which uses the embedding of the quotient unit into the dual of a compact tensored with itself; then it shows that both kernels of f and g would have to be contained in the unique maximal tensor-ideal, forcing a monomorphism into a tensor product of flat objects and contradicting f tensor g = 0. The converse direction uses E_B tensor E_C = 0 for distinct homological primes, finite presentability of the unit to factor the units of the pure-injectives through compacts, and the weak-ring property to convert nilpotence into E_B tensor z = 0. Neither implication is a formal consequence of the definitions, and the appendix theorem is the paper's only unconditional characterization of injectivity of the comparison map.
